celaleyn:43-43.t: ﴿إِذْ يُرِيكَهُمُ اللَّهُ فِي مَنَامِكَ﴾ i.e. your sleep ﴿قَلِيلًا﴾ so you informed your Companions of it and they were glad. ﴿وَلَوْ أَرَاكَهُمْ كَثِيرًا لَفَشِلْتُمْ﴾ you would have fallen into disagreement ﴿وَلَتَنَازَعْتُمْ فِي الْأَمْرِ﴾ the matter of fighting ﴿وَلَكِنَّ اللَّهَ سَلَّمَ﴾ you from losing heart and from disputing. ﴿إِنَّهُ عَلِيمٌ بِذَاتِ الصُّدُورِ﴾ of what is in the hearts.

celaleyn:44-44.t: ﴿وَإِذْ يُرِيكُمُوهُمْ﴾ O believers, ﴿إِذِ الْتَقَيْتُمْ فِي أَعْيُنِكُمْ قَلِيلًا﴾ around seventy or a hundred, when they were a thousand, so that you would advance against them; ﴿وَيُقَلِّلُكُمْ فِي أَعْيُنِهِمْ﴾ so that they would advance and not turn back from fighting them. This was before the battle was joined; when it was joined, He showed them [Translator's note: the believers] to them as twice their number, as in Āl ʿImrān. ﴿لِيَقْضِيَ اللَّهُ أَمْرًا كَانَ مَفْعُولًا وَإِلَى اللَّهِ تُرْجَعُ الْأُمُورُ﴾

celaleyn:45-45.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِذَا لَقِيتُمْ فِئَةً﴾ an unbelieving band ﴿فَاثْبُتُوا﴾ in fighting them and do not flee; ﴿وَاذْكُرُوا اللَّهَ كَثِيرًا﴾ call upon Him for victory, ﴿لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ﴾ you will triumph.

celaleyn:46-46.t: ﴿وَأَطِيعُوا اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ وَلَا تَنَازَعُوا﴾ do not disagree among yourselves ﴿فَتَفْشَلُوا﴾ and lose courage ﴿وَتَذْهَبَ رِيحُكُمْ﴾ your strength and your power; ﴿وَاصْبِرُوا إِنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَ الصَّابِرِينَ﴾ with victory and help.

celaleyn:47-47.t: ﴿وَلَا تَكُونُوا كَالَّذِينَ خَرَجُوا مِنْ دِيَارِهِمْ﴾ to protect others [Translator's note: i.e. their caravan], and did not return after it had escaped, ﴿بَطَرًا وَرِئَاءَ النَّاسِ﴾ since they said: "We will not return until we drink wine, slaughter camels and singing-girls play for us at Badr, so that people hear of it from one another," ﴿وَيَصُدُّونَ﴾ people ﴿عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ وَاللَّهُ بِمَا يَعْمَلُونَ﴾ with yāʾ and with tāʾ [Translator's note: i.e. read both "they do" and "you do"] ﴿مُحِيطٌ﴾ in knowledge, so He will requite them for it.

celaleyn:48-48.t: ﴿وَ﴾ remember ﴿إِذْ زَيَّنَ لَهُمُ الشَّيْطَانُ﴾ Iblīs ﴿أَعْمَالَهُمْ﴾ by encouraging them to meet the Muslims, when they feared setting out because of their enemies, the Banū Bakr, ﴿وَقَالَ﴾ to them: ﴿لَا غَالِبَ لَكُمُ الْيَوْمَ مِنَ النَّاسِ وَإِنِّي جَارٌ لَكُمْ﴾ against Kināna; he had come to them in the form of Surāqa ibn Mālik, the chief of that region. ﴿فَلَمَّا تَرَاءَتِ﴾ met ﴿الْفِئَتَانِ﴾ the Muslim and the unbelieving one, and he saw the angels, while his hand was in the hand of al-Ḥārith ibn Hishām, ﴿نَكَصَ﴾ he turned back ﴿عَلَى عَقِبَيْهِ﴾ fleeing, ﴿وَقَالَ﴾ when they said to him, "Will you forsake us in this state?": ﴿إِنِّي بَرِيءٌ مِنْكُمْ﴾ from my protection of you; ﴿إِنِّي أَرَى مَا لَا تَرَوْنَ﴾ of the angels; ﴿إِنِّي أَخَافُ اللَّهَ﴾ that He will destroy me; ﴿وَاللَّهُ شَدِيدُ الْعِقَابِ﴾

celaleyn:49-49.t: ﴿إِذْ يَقُولُ الْمُنَافِقُونَ وَالَّذِينَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ مَرَضٌ﴾ weakness of belief: ﴿غَرَّ هَؤُلَاءِ﴾ i.e. the Muslims ﴿دِينُهُمْ﴾ since they went out, few as they were, to fight the great host, imagining that they would be given victory because of it. Allah the Exalted said in reply to them: ﴿وَمَنْ يَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى اللَّهِ﴾ trusts in Him, will prevail; ﴿فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ﴾ prevailing over His affair, ﴿حَكِيمٌ﴾ in His making.

celaleyn:50-50.t: ﴿وَلَوْ تَرَى﴾ O Muḥammad, ﴿إِذْ يَتَوَفَّى﴾ with yāʾ and with tāʾ ﴿الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا الْمَلَائِكَةُ يَضْرِبُونَ﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial) ﴿وُجُوهَهُمْ وَأَدْبَارَهُمْ﴾ with iron maces, ﴿وَ﴾ saying to them: ﴿ذُوقُوا عَذَابَ الْحَرِيقِ﴾ i.e. the Fire. The answer of لَوْ is: "you would have seen a tremendous thing".

celaleyn:51-51.t: ﴿ذَلِكَ﴾ punishment ﴿بِمَا قَدَّمَتْ أَيْدِيكُمْ﴾ they [Translator's note: the hands] are mentioned rather than anything else because most deeds are performed with them; ﴿وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ لَيْسَ بِظَلَّامٍ﴾ i.e. one who does injustice ﴿لِلْعَبِيدِ﴾ so that He would punish them without a sin. The way of these is

celaleyn:52-52.t: ﴿كَدَأْبِ﴾ like the custom of ﴿آلِ فِرْعَوْنَ وَالَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ كَفَرُوا بِآيَاتِ اللَّهِ فَأَخَذَهُمُ اللَّهُ﴾ with punishment ﴿بِذُنُوبِهِمْ﴾ — the clause كَفَرُوا and what follows it explains what precedes it. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ قَوِيٌّ﴾ over what He wills, ﴿شَدِيدُ الْعِقَابِ﴾

celaleyn:53-53.t: ﴿ذَلِكَ﴾ i.e. the punishment of the unbelievers, ﴿بِأَنَّ﴾ i.e. because ﴿اللَّهَ لَمْ يَكُ مُغَيِّرًا نِعْمَةً أَنْعَمَهَا عَلَى قَوْمٍ﴾ replacing it with retribution ﴿حَتَّى يُغَيِّرُوا مَا بِأَنْفُسِهِمْ﴾ replace their blessing with unbelief, as the unbelievers of Mecca replaced His feeding them against hunger, His securing them from fear and His sending the Prophet ﷺ to them, with unbelief, barring from the way of Allah and fighting the believers. ﴿وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ﴾

celaleyn:54-54.t: ﴿كَدَأْبِ آلِ فِرْعَوْنَ وَالَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ كَذَّبُوا بِآيَاتِ رَبِّهِمْ فَأَهْلَكْنَاهُمْ بِذُنُوبِهِمْ وَأَغْرَقْنَا آلَ فِرْعَوْنَ﴾ his people along with him; ﴿وَكُلٌّ﴾ of the nations that gave the lie ﴿كَانُوا ظَالِمِينَ﴾. And there was revealed concerning Qurayẓa:

celaleyn:55-55.t: ﴿إِنَّ شَرَّ الدَّوَابِّ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا فَهُمْ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:56-56.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ عَاهَدْتَ مِنْهُمْ﴾ that they would not aid the idolaters, ﴿ثُمَّ يَنْقُضُونَ عَهْدَهُمْ فِي كُلِّ مَرَّةٍ﴾ in which they made a covenant, ﴿وَهُمْ لَا يَتَّقُونَ﴾ Allah in their treachery.

celaleyn:57-57.t: ﴿فَإِمَّا﴾ in it is the assimilation (idghām) of the nūn of the conditional إِنْ into the redundant (zāʾida) مَا, ﴿تَثْقَفَنَّهُمْ﴾ you find them ﴿فِي الْحَرْبِ فَشَرِّدْ﴾ scatter ﴿بِهِمْ مَنْ خَلْفَهُمْ﴾ of the combatants, by making an example of them and punishing them, ﴿لَعَلَّهُمْ﴾ i.e. those behind them ﴿يَذَّكَّرُونَ﴾ take warning from them.

celaleyn:58-58.t: ﴿وَإِمَّا تَخَافَنَّ مِنْ قَوْمٍ﴾ who have made a covenant with you ﴿خِيَانَةً﴾ in a covenant, through a sign that appears to you, ﴿فَانْبِذْ﴾ throw back their covenant ﴿إِلَيْهِمْ عَلَى سَوَاءٍ﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. you and they being equal in knowing of the covenant's dissolution, by your informing them of it, so that they do not accuse you of treachery. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ الْخَائِنِينَ﴾ And there was revealed concerning those who escaped on the day of Badr:

celaleyn:59-59.t: ﴿وَلَا تَحْسَبَنَّ﴾ O Muḥammad, ﴿الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا سَبَقُوا﴾ Allah, i.e. escaped Him; ﴿إِنَّهُمْ لَا يُعْجِزُونَ﴾ they do not escape Him. In one reading it is with the lower-dotted letter [Translator's note: yāʾ: يَحْسَبَنَّ], in which case the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object) is omitted, i.e. "themselves"; and in another with أَنَّ given fatḥa, on the implied (muqaddar) lām [Translator's note: i.e. "because they …"].

celaleyn:60-60.t: ﴿وَأَعِدُّوا لَهُمْ﴾ for fighting them ﴿مَا اسْتَطَعْتُمْ مِنْ قُوَّةٍ﴾ — he ﷺ said: "It is shooting." Narrated by Muslim. ﴿وَمِنْ رِبَاطِ الْخَيْلِ﴾ a maṣdar (verbal noun) meaning keeping them tethered in the way of Allah, ﴿تُرْهِبُونَ﴾ you frighten ﴿بِهِ عَدُوَّ اللَّهِ وَعَدُوَّكُمْ﴾ i.e. the unbelievers of Mecca, ﴿وَآخَرِينَ مِنْ دُونِهِمْ﴾ i.e. others besides them, namely the hypocrites or the Jews; ﴿لَا تَعْلَمُونَهُمُ اللَّهُ يَعْلَمُهُمْ وَمَا تُنْفِقُوا مِنْ شَيْءٍ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ يُوَفَّ إِلَيْكُمْ﴾ its reward, ﴿وَأَنْتُمْ لَا تُظْلَمُونَ﴾ you will not be diminished anything of it.

celaleyn:61-61.t: ﴿وَإِنْ جَنَحُوا﴾ incline ﴿لِلسِّلْمِ﴾ with kasra and fatḥa on the sīn [لِلسَّلْمِ]: peace, ﴿فَاجْنَحْ لَهَا﴾ and make a covenant with them. Ibn ʿAbbās said: this is abrogated by the Verse of the Sword; and Mujāhid said: it is specific to the People of the Book, since it was revealed concerning the Banū Qurayẓa. ﴿وَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى اللَّهِ﴾ trust in Him; ﴿إِنَّهُ هُوَ السَّمِيعُ﴾ of speech, ﴿الْعَلِيمُ﴾ of action.

celaleyn:62-62.t: ﴿وَإِنْ يُرِيدُوا أَنْ يَخْدَعُوكَ﴾ by the peace, in order to prepare against you, ﴿فَإِنَّ حَسْبَكَ﴾ sufficient for you is ﴿اللَّهُ هُوَ الَّذِي أَيَّدَكَ بِنَصْرِهِ وَبِالْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾

celaleyn:63-63.t: ﴿وَأَلَّفَ﴾ brought together ﴿بَيْنَ قُلُوبِهِمْ﴾ after the rancours; ﴿لَوْ أَنْفَقْتَ مَا فِي الْأَرْضِ جَمِيعًا مَا أَلَّفْتَ بَيْنَ قُلُوبِهِمْ وَلَكِنَّ اللَّهَ أَلَّفَ بَيْنَهُمْ﴾ by His power. ﴿إِنَّهُ عَزِيزٌ﴾ prevailing over His affair, ﴿حَكِيمٌ﴾ nothing goes outside His wisdom.

celaleyn:64-64.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ حَسْبُكَ اللَّهُ وَ﴾ sufficient for you is ﴿مَنِ اتَّبَعَكَ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾

celaleyn:65-65.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ حَرِّضِ﴾ urge ﴿الْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَى الْقِتَالِ﴾ of the unbelievers. ﴿إِنْ يَكُنْ مِنْكُمْ عِشْرُونَ صَابِرُونَ يَغْلِبُوا مِائَتَيْنِ﴾ of them, ﴿وَإِنْ يَكُنْ﴾ with yāʾ and with tāʾ ﴿مِنْكُمْ مِائَةٌ يَغْلِبُوا أَلْفًا مِنَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِأَنَّهُمْ﴾ i.e. because they are ﴿قَوْمٌ لَا يَفْقَهُونَ﴾. This is a statement (khabar) with the meaning of a command, i.e. let the twenty of you fight the two hundred and the hundred a thousand, and stand firm against them. Then it was abrogated, when they became many, by His saying:

celaleyn:66-66.t: ﴿الْآنَ خَفَّفَ اللَّهُ عَنْكُمْ وَعَلِمَ أَنَّ فِيكُمْ ضُعْفًا﴾ with ḍamma and fatḥa on the ḍād [ضَعْفًا], in fighting ten times your number. ﴿فَإِنْ يَكُنْ﴾ with yāʾ and with tāʾ ﴿مِنْكُمْ مِائَةٌ صَابِرَةٌ يَغْلِبُوا مِائَتَيْنِ﴾ of them, ﴿وَإِنْ يَكُنْ مِنْكُمْ أَلْفٌ يَغْلِبُوا أَلْفَيْنِ بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ﴾ by His will. It is a statement (khabar) with the meaning of a command, i.e. fight twice your number and stand firm against them. ﴿وَاللَّهُ مَعَ الصَّابِرِينَ﴾ with His help. And there was revealed, when they took ransom from the captives of Badr:

celaleyn:67-67.t: ﴿مَا كَانَ لِنَبِيٍّ أَنْ تَكُونَ﴾ with tāʾ and with yāʾ [يَكُونَ] ﴿لَهُ أَسْرَى حَتَّى يُثْخِنَ فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ goes to the utmost in killing the unbelievers. ﴿تُرِيدُونَ﴾ O believers, ﴿عَرَضَ الدُّنْيَا﴾ its fleeting debris, by taking ransom, ﴿وَاللَّهُ يُرِيدُ﴾ for you ﴿الْآخِرَةَ﴾ i.e. its reward, by your killing them; ﴿وَاللَّهُ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ﴾. This is abrogated by His saying {فَإِمَّا مَنًّا بَعْدُ وَإِمَّا فِدَاءً} ("then either grace afterwards or ransom").

celaleyn:68-68.t: ﴿لَوْلَا كِتَابٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ سَبَقَ﴾ in making the spoils and the captives lawful for you, ﴿لَمَسَّكُمْ فِيمَا أَخَذْتُمْ﴾ of the ransom ﴿عَذَابٌ عَظِيمٌ﴾

celaleyn:69-69.t: ﴿فَكُلُوا مِمَّا غَنِمْتُمْ حَلَالًا طَيِّبًا وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:70-70.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ قُلْ لِمَنْ فِي أَيْدِيكُمْ مِنَ الْأَسَارَى﴾ and in one reading [الْأَسْرَى]: ﴿إِنْ يَعْلَمِ اللَّهُ فِي قُلُوبِكُمْ خَيْرًا﴾ faith and sincerity, ﴿يُؤْتِكُمْ خَيْرًا مِمَّا أُخِذَ مِنْكُمْ﴾ of the ransom, by multiplying it for you in this world and rewarding you in the Hereafter, ﴿وَيَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ﴾ your sins; ﴿وَاللَّهُ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾

celaleyn:71-71.t: ﴿وَإِنْ يُرِيدُوا﴾ i.e. the captives ﴿خِيَانَتَكَ﴾ by what they have professed in speech, ﴿فَقَدْ خَانُوا اللَّهَ مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾ before Badr, by unbelief, ﴿فَأَمْكَنَ مِنْهُمْ﴾ at Badr, by killing and capture; so let them expect the like of that if they return [Translator's note: to it]. ﴿وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ﴾ of His creation, ﴿حَكِيمٌ﴾ in His making.

celaleyn:72-72.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَهَاجَرُوا وَجَاهَدُوا بِأَمْوَالِهِمْ وَأَنْفُسِهِمْ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ﴾ — they are the Emigrants (al-Muhājirūn) — ﴿وَالَّذِينَ آوَوْا﴾ the Prophet ﷺ ﴿وَنَصَرُوا﴾ — they are the Helpers (al-Anṣār) — ﴿أُولَئِكَ بَعْضُهُمْ أَوْلِيَاءُ بَعْضٍ﴾ in support and inheritance. ﴿وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَلَمْ يُهَاجِرُوا مَا لَكُمْ مِنْ وِلَايَتِهِمْ﴾ with kasra and fatḥa on the wāw [وَلَايَتِهِمْ] ﴿مِنْ شَيْءٍ﴾ so there is no inheritance between you and them, and no share for them in the spoils, ﴿حَتَّى يُهَاجِرُوا﴾. This is abrogated by the end of the surah. ﴿وَإِنِ اسْتَنْصَرُوكُمْ فِي الدِّينِ فَعَلَيْكُمُ النَّصْرُ﴾ for them against the unbelievers, ﴿إِلَّا عَلَى قَوْمٍ بَيْنَكُمْ وَبَيْنَهُمْ مِيثَاقٌ﴾ a covenant: then do not help them against them and break your covenant with them. ﴿وَاللَّهُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ﴾

celaleyn:73-73.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بَعْضُهُمْ أَوْلِيَاءُ بَعْضٍ﴾ in support and inheritance, so there is no inheritance between you and them. ﴿إِلَّا تَفْعَلُوهُ﴾ i.e. befriending the Muslims and cutting off the unbelievers, ﴿تَكُنْ فِتْنَةٌ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَفَسَادٌ كَبِيرٌ﴾ through the strength of unbelief and the weakness of Islam.

celaleyn:74-74.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَهَاجَرُوا وَجَاهَدُوا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ وَالَّذِينَ آوَوْا وَنَصَرُوا أُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ حَقًّا لَهُمْ مَغْفِرَةٌ وَرِزْقٌ كَرِيمٌ﴾ in Paradise.

celaleyn:75-75.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا مِنْ بَعْدُ﴾ i.e. after those who were first to faith and emigration, ﴿وَهَاجَرُوا وَجَاهَدُوا مَعَكُمْ فَأُولَئِكَ مِنْكُمْ﴾ O Emigrants and Helpers. ﴿وَأُولُوا الْأَرْحَامِ﴾ those of kinship ﴿بَعْضُهُمْ أَوْلَى بِبَعْضٍ﴾ in inheritance than inheritance through faith and emigration mentioned in the previous ayah, ﴿فِي كِتَابِ اللَّهِ﴾ the Preserved Tablet. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ﴾ and part of that is the wisdom of inheritance.

celaleyn:1-1.t: When the Muslims disagreed about the spoils of Badr — the young men said, "They are ours, because we engaged in the fighting," and the old men said, "We were a support for you beneath the banners; had you been routed you would have fallen back to us, so do not take them for yourselves" — there was revealed: ﴿يَسْأَلُونَكَ﴾ O Muḥammad ﴿عَنِ الْأَنْفَالِ﴾ the spoils, whose they are ﴿قُلْ﴾ to them ﴿الْأَنْفَالُ لِلَّهِ﴾ He assigns them wherever He wills ﴿وَالرَّسُولِ﴾ he divides them by Allah's command. So he ﷺ divided them among them equally; al-Ḥākim narrated it in al-Mustadrak ﴿فَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَأَصْلِحُوا ذَاتَ بَيْنِكُمْ﴾ i.e. the reality of what is between you, through affection and abandoning dispute ﴿وَأَطِيعُوا اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ truly

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿إِنَّمَا الْمُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ those complete in faith ﴿الَّذِينَ إِذَا ذُكِرَ اللَّهُ﴾ i.e. His threat ﴿وَجِلَتْ﴾ fear ﴿قُلُوبُهُمْ وَإِذَا تُلِيَتْ عَلَيْهِمْ آيَاتُهُ زَادَتْهُمْ إِيمَانًا﴾ assent ﴿وَعَلَى رَبِّهِمْ يَتَوَكَّلُونَ﴾ in Him they trust, not in another

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ يُقِيمُونَ الصَّلَوةَ﴾ perform it with its rights ﴿وَمِمَّا رَزَقْنَاهُمْ﴾ We have given them ﴿يُنْفِقُونَ﴾ in obedience to Allah

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿أُولَئِكَ﴾ those described by what has been mentioned ﴿هُمُ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ حَقًّا﴾ truly, without doubt ﴿لَهُمْ دَرَجَاتٌ﴾ ranks in the Garden ﴿عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ وَمَغْفِرَةٌ وَرِزْقٌ كَرِيمٌ﴾ in the Garden

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿كَمَا أَخْرَجَكَ رَبُّكَ مِنْ بَيْتِكَ بِالْحَقِّ﴾ attached to (mutaʿalliq) أَخْرَجَ ﴿وَإِنَّ فَرِيقًا مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ لَكَارِهُونَ﴾ the going out. The clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the kāf of أَخْرَجَكَ, and كَمَا is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. this state, in their disliking it, is like your being brought out while they disliked it — and it was better for them; so likewise this. That was because Abū Sufyān came with a caravan from Syria, and the Prophet ﷺ and his companions went out to take it as spoil. Quraysh learned of it, and Abū Jahl and the fighters of Mecca went out to defend it — they are al-Nafīr (the armed force). Abū Sufyān took the caravan along the coastal road and it escaped. It was said to Abū Jahl, "Go back," but he refused and marched to Badr. The Prophet ﷺ consulted his companions and said: "Allah has promised me one of the two parties." They agreed with him on fighting al-Nafīr, though some of them disliked that and said, "We have not prepared for it," as the Exalted said:

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿يُجَادِلُونَكَ فِي الْحَقِّ﴾ the fighting ﴿بَعْدَ مَا تَبَيَّنَ﴾ became clear to them ﴿كَأَنَّمَا يُسَاقُونَ إِلَى الْمَوْتِ وَهُمْ يَنْظُرُونَ﴾ at it, openly — in their dislike of it

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿وَ﴾ remember ﴿إِذْ يَعِدُكُمُ اللَّهُ إِحْدَى الطَّائِفَتَيْنِ﴾ the caravan or al-Nafīr ﴿أَنَّهَا لَكُمْ وَتَوَدُّونَ﴾ you wish ﴿أَنَّ غَيْرَ ذَاتِ الشَّوْكَةِ﴾ i.e. of might and weapons, which is the caravan ﴿تَكُونُ لَكُمْ﴾ because of the smallness of its numbers and supplies, unlike al-Nafīr ﴿وَيُرِيدُ اللَّهُ أَنْ يُحِقَّ الْحَقَّ﴾ make it manifest ﴿بِكَلِمَاتِهِ﴾ His prior words concerning the victory of Islam ﴿وَيَقْطَعَ دَابِرَ الْكَافِرِينَ﴾ the last of them, by extirpation; so He commanded you to fight al-Nafīr

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿لِيُحِقَّ الْحَقَّ وَيُبْطِلَ﴾ obliterate ﴿الْبَاطِلَ﴾ disbelief ﴿وَلَوْ كَرِهَ الْمُجْرِمُونَ﴾ the polytheists, that

celaleyn:9-9.t: Remember ﴿إِذْ تَسْتَغِيثُونَ رَبَّكُمْ﴾ seek His rescue by victory over them ﴿فَاسْتَجَابَ لَكُمْ أَنِّي﴾ i.e. بِأَنِّي ("that I") ﴿مُمِدُّكُمْ﴾ will help you ﴿بِأَلْفٍ مِنَ الْمَلَائِكَةِ مُرْدِفِينَ﴾ in succession, some following others. He promised them this first, then it became three thousand, then five, as in Āl ʿImrān. It was also read بِآلُفٍ, like أَفْلُس, a plural.

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿وَمَا جَعَلَهُ اللَّهُ﴾ i.e. the reinforcement ﴿إِلَّا بُشْرَى وَلِتَطْمَئِنَّ بِهِ قُلُوبُكُمْ وَمَا النَّصْرُ إِلَّا مِنْ عِنْدِ اللَّهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ﴾ Remember

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿إِذْ يُغَشَّاكُمُ النُّعَاسُ أَمَنَةً﴾ security from the fear that had come upon you; [يُغَشِّيكُمْ] ﴿مِنْهُ﴾ the Exalted ﴿وَيُنَزِّلُ عَلَيْكُمْ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مَاءً لِيُطَهِّرَكُمْ بِهِ﴾ from minor impurities and major ritual impurity (janāba) ﴿وَيُذْهِبَ عَنْكُمْ رِجْزَ الشَّيْطَانِ﴾ his whispering to you that if you were in the right you would not be thirsty and in a state of impurity while the polytheists held the water ﴿وَلِيَرْبِطَ﴾ hold firm ﴿عَلَى قُلُوبِكُمْ﴾ with certainty and patience ﴿وَيُثَبِّتَ بِهِ الْأَقْدَامَ﴾ from sinking in the sand

celaleyn:12-12.t: ﴿إِذْ يُوحِي رَبُّكَ إِلَى الْمَلَائِكَةِ﴾ with whom He reinforced the Muslims ﴿أَنِّي﴾ i.e. بِأَنِّي ("that I") ﴿مَعَكُمْ﴾ with help and victory ﴿فَثَبِّتُوا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ by aiding and giving glad tidings ﴿سَأُلْقِي فِي قُلُوبِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا الرُّعْبَ﴾ fear ﴿فَاضْرِبُوا فَوْقَ الْأَعْنَاقِ﴾ i.e. the heads ﴿وَاضْرِبُوا مِنْهُمْ كُلَّ بَنَانٍ﴾ i.e. the extremities of the hands and feet. A man would aim to strike the neck of a disbeliever and it would fall before his sword reached him. And he ﷺ threw a handful of pebbles at them, and not a polytheist remained but some of it entered his eyes, and they were routed.

celaleyn:13-13.t: ﴿ذَلِكَ﴾ the punishment that befell them ﴿بِأَنَّهُمْ شَاقُّوا﴾ opposed ﴿اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ وَمَنْ يُشَاقِقِ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ شَدِيدُ الْعِقَابِ﴾ to him

celaleyn:14-14.t: ﴿ذَلِكُمْ﴾ the punishment ﴿فَذُوقُوهُ﴾ O disbelievers, in this world ﴿وَأَنَّ لِلْكَافِرِينَ﴾ in the Hereafter ﴿عَذَابَ النَّارِ﴾

celaleyn:15-15.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِذَا لَقِيتُمُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا زَحْفًا﴾ i.e. massed, as though, by their great numbers, they were creeping ﴿فَلَا تُوَلُّوهُمُ الْأَدْبَارَ﴾ in rout

celaleyn:16-16.t: ﴿وَمَنْ يُوَلِّهِمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾ i.e. on the day of meeting them ﴿دُبُرَهُ إِلَّا مُتَحَرِّفًا﴾ turning aside ﴿لِقِتَالٍ﴾ by showing them flight as a stratagem while intending to return to the attack ﴿أَوْ مُتَحَيِّزًا﴾ joining ﴿إِلَى فِئَةٍ﴾ a group of Muslims whose help he seeks ﴿فَقَدْ بَاءَ﴾ has returned ﴿بِغَضَبٍ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَمَأْوَاهُ جَهَنَّمُ وَبِئْسَ الْمَصِيرُ﴾ the destination is it. This is restricted to when the disbelievers do not exceed double.

celaleyn:17-17.t: ﴿فَلَمْ تَقْتُلُوهُمْ﴾ at Badr by your own strength ﴿وَلَكِنَّ اللَّهَ قَتَلَهُمْ﴾ by His granting you victory ﴿وَمَا رَمَيْتَ﴾ O Muḥammad, the eyes of the people ﴿إِذْ رَمَيْتَ﴾ with the pebbles, because a handful of pebbles does not fill the eyes of a large army by a human throw ﴿وَلَكِنَّ اللَّهَ رَمَى﴾ by making it reach them. He did that to subdue the disbelievers ﴿وَلِيُبْلِيَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ مِنْهُ بَلَاءً﴾ a gift ﴿حَسَنًا﴾ which is the spoils ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ سَمِيعٌ﴾ of their words ﴿عَلِيمٌ﴾ of their states

celaleyn:18-18.t: ﴿ذَلِكُمْ﴾ the bestowal is true ﴿وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ مُوهِنُ﴾ weakens ﴿كَيْدِ الْكَافِرِينَ﴾

celaleyn:19-19.t: ﴿إِنْ تَسْتَفْتِحُوا﴾ O disbelievers, i.e. if you seek the فَتْح, i.e. the judgement — when Abū Jahl among you said: "O Allah, whichever of us was more given to severing kinship and brought us what we do not know, destroy him (aḥinhu) this morning," i.e. annihilate him ﴿فَقَدْ جَاءَكُمُ الْفَتْحُ﴾ the judgement, by the destruction of whoever was like that, namely Abū Jahl and those killed with him, not the Prophet ﷺ and the believers ﴿وَإِنْ تَنْتَهُوا﴾ from disbelief and war ﴿فَهُوَ خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ وَإِنْ تَعُودُوا﴾ to fighting the Prophet ﷺ ﴿نَعُدْ﴾ to giving him victory over you ﴿وَلَنْ تُغْنِيَ﴾ ward off ﴿عَنْكُمْ فِئَتُكُمْ﴾ your groups ﴿شَيْئًا وَلَوْ كَثُرَتْ وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ with kasra on إِنَّ as a resumption (istiʾnāf), and with fatḥa [وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ] on the assumption of an implied lām

celaleyn:20-20.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَطِيعُوا اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ وَلَا تَوَلَّوْا﴾ turn away ﴿عَنْهُ﴾ by opposing his command ﴿وَأَنْتُمْ تَسْمَعُونَ﴾ the Quran and the admonitions

celaleyn:21-21.t: ﴿وَلَا تَكُونُوا كَالَّذِينَ قَالُوا سَمِعْنَا وَهُمْ لَا يَسْمَعُونَ﴾ with a hearing of reflection and taking admonition; they are the hypocrites or the polytheists

celaleyn:22-22.t: ﴿إِنَّ شَرَّ الدَّوَابِّ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ الصُّمُّ﴾ to hearing the truth ﴿الْبُكْمُ﴾ to speaking it ﴿الَّذِينَ لَا يَعْقِلُونَ﴾

celaleyn:23-23.t: ﴿وَلَوْ عَلِمَ اللَّهُ فِيهِمْ خَيْرًا﴾ soundness, through hearing the truth ﴿لَأَسْمَعَهُمْ﴾ a hearing of understanding ﴿وَلَوْ أَسْمَعَهُمْ﴾ supposing so, when He has known that there is no good in them ﴿لَتَوَلَّوْا﴾ from it ﴿وَهُمْ مُعْرِضُونَ﴾ from accepting it, out of obstinacy and denial

celaleyn:24-24.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اسْتَجِيبُوا لِلَّهِ وَلِلرَّسُولِ﴾ with obedience ﴿إِذَا دَعَاكُمْ لِمَا يُحْيِيكُمْ﴾ of the matter of religion, because it is the cause of eternal life ﴿وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ يَحُولُ بَيْنَ الْمَرْءِ وَقَلْبِهِ﴾ so he cannot believe or disbelieve except by His will ﴿وَأَنَّهُ إِلَيْهِ تُحْشَرُونَ﴾ and He will recompense you for your deeds

celaleyn:25-25.t: ﴿وَاتَّقُوا فِتْنَةً﴾ which, if it strikes you, ﴿لَا تُصِيبَنَّ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا مِنْكُمْ خَاصَّةً﴾ but will include them and others; guarding against it is by disavowing the wrongdoing that brings it about ﴿وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ شَدِيدُ الْعِقَابِ﴾ for whoever opposes Him

celaleyn:26-26.t: ﴿وَاذْكُرُوا إِذْ أَنْتُمْ قَلِيلٌ مُسْتَضْعَفُونَ فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ the land of Mecca ﴿تَخَافُونَ أَنْ يَتَخَطَّفَكُمُ النَّاسُ﴾ the disbelievers seize you swiftly ﴿فَآوَاكُمْ﴾ to Medina ﴿وَأَيَّدَكُمْ﴾ strengthened you ﴿بِنَصْرِهِ﴾ on the day of Badr, with the angels ﴿وَرَزَقَكُمْ مِنَ الطَّيِّبَاتِ﴾ the spoils ﴿لَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ﴾ His blessings. And there was revealed concerning Abū Lubāba Marwān ibn ʿAbd al-Mundhir — he ﷺ had sent him to Banū Qurayẓa so that they would submit to his judgement; they consulted him, and he indicated to them that it would be slaughter, because his family and wealth were among them —

celaleyn:27-27.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا تَخُونُوا اللَّهَ وَالرَّسُولَ﴾ and do not ﴿وَتَخُونُوا أَمَانَاتِكُمْ﴾ what you have been entrusted with, of religion and other things ﴿وَأَنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ﴾

celaleyn:28-28.t: ﴿وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّمَا أَمْوَالُكُمْ وَأَوْلَادُكُمْ فِتْنَةٌ﴾ for you, turning you away from the affairs of the Hereafter ﴿وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ عِنْدَهُ أَجْرٌ عَظِيمٌ﴾ so do not miss it by attending to wealth and children and by betraying for their sake. And there was revealed concerning his repentance:

celaleyn:29-29.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِنْ تَتَّقُوا اللَّهَ﴾ by turning back to Him and otherwise ﴿يَجْعَلْ لَكُمْ فُرْقَانًا﴾ between you and what you fear, so that you are saved ﴿وَيُكَفِّرْ عَنْكُمْ سَيِّئَاتِكُمْ وَيَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ﴾ your sins ﴿وَاللَّهُ ذُو الْفَضْلِ الْعَظِيمِ﴾

celaleyn:30-30.t: ﴿وَ﴾ remember, O Muḥammad, ﴿إِذْ يَمْكُرُ بِكَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾ when they had gathered in Dār al-Nadwa to consult about you ﴿لِيُثْبِتُوكَ﴾ bind and imprison you ﴿أَوْ يَقْتُلُوكَ﴾ all of them, as the killing of one man ﴿أَوْ يُخْرِجُوكَ﴾ from Mecca ﴿وَيَمْكُرُونَ﴾ against you ﴿وَيَمْكُرُ اللَّهُ﴾ against them, by arranging your affair: He revealed to you what they had planned and commanded you to leave ﴿وَاللَّهُ خَيْرُ الْمَاكِرِينَ﴾ the most knowing of them in it

celaleyn:31-31.t: ﴿وَإِذَا تُتْلَى عَلَيْهِمْ آيَاتُنَا﴾ the Quran ﴿قَالُوا قَدْ سَمِعْنَا لَوْ نَشَاءُ لَقُلْنَا مِثْلَ هَذَا﴾ Al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith said it, because he used to go to al-Ḥīra to trade, buy books of the reports of the Persians, and relate them to the people of Mecca ﴿إِنْ﴾ this is not ﴿هَذَا﴾ Quran ﴿إِلَّا أَسَاطِيرُ﴾ the lies of ﴿الْأَوَّلِينَ﴾

celaleyn:32-32.t: ﴿وَإِذْ قَالُوا اللَّهُمَّ إِنْ كَانَ هَذَا﴾ which Muḥammad recites ﴿هُوَ الْحَقَّ﴾ sent down ﴿مِنْ عِنْدِكَ فَأَمْطِرْ عَلَيْنَا حِجَارَةً مِنَ السَّمَاءِ أَوِ ائْتِنَا بِعَذَابٍ أَلِيمٍ﴾ painful, for denying it. Al-Naḍr or someone else said it in mockery, and to give the impression that he had clear insight and certainty of its falsehood. The Exalted said:

celaleyn:33-33.t: ﴿وَمَا كَانَ اللَّهُ لِيُعَذِّبَهُمْ﴾ with what they asked for ﴿وَأَنْتَ فِيهِمْ﴾ because when punishment descends it is general, and no community was punished except after its prophet and the believers had left it ﴿وَمَا كَانَ اللَّهُ مُعَذِّبَهُمْ وَهُمْ يَسْتَغْفِرُونَ﴾ in that they say in their circumambulation, "Your forgiveness! Your forgiveness!" It is also said: they are the oppressed believers among them, as the Exalted said: {لَوْ تَزَيَّلُوا لَعَذَّبْنَا الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنْهُمْ عَذَابًا أَلِيمًا}

celaleyn:34-34.t: ﴿وَمَا لَهُمْ أَ﴾ -n ﴿لَا يُعَذِّبَهُمُ اللَّهُ﴾ with the sword, after your departure and that of the oppressed. On the first view it abrogates what precedes it; and Allah did punish them at Badr and elsewhere ﴿وَهُمْ يَصُدُّونَ﴾ prevent the Prophet ﷺ and the Muslims ﴿عَنِ الْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرَامِ﴾ from circumambulating it ﴿وَمَا كَانُوا أَوْلِيَاءَهُ﴾ as they claimed ﴿إِنْ﴾ its guardians are not ﴿أَوْلِيَاؤُهُ إِلَّا الْمُتَّقُونَ وَلَكِنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ that they have no guardianship over it

celaleyn:35-35.t: ﴿وَمَا كَانَ صَلَاتُهُمْ عِنْدَ الْبَيْتِ إِلَّا مُكَاءً﴾ whistling ﴿وَتَصْدِيَةً﴾ clapping, i.e. they made that take the place of the prayer they were commanded to perform ﴿فَذُوقُوا الْعَذَابَ﴾ at Badr ﴿بِمَا كُنْتُمْ تَكْفُرُونَ﴾

celaleyn:36-36.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا يُنْفِقُونَ أَمْوَالَهُمْ﴾ in war against the Prophet ﷺ ﴿لِيَصُدُّوا عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ فَسَيُنْفِقُونَهَا ثُمَّ تَكُونُ﴾ in the outcome of the affair ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ حَسْرَةً﴾ regret, at its loss and the loss of what they aimed at ﴿ثُمَّ يُغْلَبُونَ﴾ in this world ﴿وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾ among them ﴿إِلَى جَهَنَّمَ﴾ in the Hereafter ﴿يُحْشَرُونَ﴾ are driven

celaleyn:37-37.t: ﴿لِيَمِيزَ﴾ attached to (mutaʿalliq) تَكُونُ; with the light and the doubled (shadda) form, i.e. separate ﴿اللَّهُ الْخَبِيثَ﴾ the disbeliever ﴿مِنَ الطَّيِّبِ﴾ the believer ﴿وَيَجْعَلَ الْخَبِيثَ بَعْضَهُ عَلَى بَعْضٍ فَيَرْكُمَهُ جَمِيعًا﴾ gather it heaped up, some upon others ﴿فَيَجْعَلَهُ فِي جَهَنَّمَ أُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْخَاسِرُونَ﴾

celaleyn:38-38.t: ﴿قُلْ لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾ such as Abū Sufyān and his companions ﴿إِنْ يَنْتَهُوا﴾ from disbelief and fighting the Prophet ﷺ ﴿يُغْفَرْ لَهُمْ مَا قَدْ سَلَفَ﴾ of their deeds ﴿وَإِنْ يَعُودُوا﴾ to fighting him ﴿فَقَدْ مَضَتْ سُنَّتُ الْأَوَّلِينَ﴾ i.e. Our way with them, by destruction; so We will do likewise with these

celaleyn:39-39.t: ﴿وَقَاتِلُوهُمْ حَتَّى لَا تَكُونَ﴾ exists ﴿فِتْنَةٌ﴾ association of partners ﴿وَيَكُونَ الدِّينُ كُلُّهُ لِلَّهِ﴾ alone, and none other is worshipped ﴿فَإِنِ انْتَهَوْا﴾ from disbelief ﴿فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ بِمَا يَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ﴾ and will recompense them for it

celaleyn:40-40.t: ﴿وَإِنْ تَوَلَّوْا﴾ from faith ﴿فَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ مَوْلَاكُمْ﴾ your helper and the One in charge of your affairs ﴿نِعْمَ الْمَوْلَى﴾ is He ﴿وَنِعْمَ النَّصِيرُ﴾ i.e. the helper for you

celaleyn:41-41.t: ﴿وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّمَا غَنِمْتُمْ﴾ took from the disbelievers by force ﴿مِنْ شَيْءٍ فَأَنَّ لِلَّهِ خُمُسَهُ﴾ He commands concerning it what He wills ﴿وَلِلرَّسُولِ وَلِذِي الْقُرْبَى﴾ the kin of the Prophet ﷺ from Banū Hāshim and Banū al-Muṭṭalib ﴿وَالْيَتَامَى﴾ the children of the Muslims whose fathers have died and who are poor ﴿وَالْمَسَاكِينِ﴾ those in need among the Muslims ﴿وَابْنِ السَّبِيلِ﴾ the one stranded on his journey among the Muslims; i.e. the Prophet ﷺ and the four categories are entitled to it according to how he used to divide it, each having a fifth of the fifth, and the remaining four fifths go to those who took the spoils ﴿إِنْ كُنْتُمْ آمَنْتُمْ بِاللَّهِ﴾ then know that ﴿وَمَا﴾ conjoined to بِاللَّهِ ﴿أَنْزَلْنَا عَلَى عَبْدِنَا﴾ Muḥammad ﷺ, of angels and signs ﴿يَوْمَ الْفُرْقَانِ﴾ i.e. the day of Badr, which separated truth from falsehood ﴿يَوْمَ الْتَقَى الْجَمْعَانِ﴾ the Muslims and the disbelievers ﴿وَاللَّهُ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ﴾ including your victory despite your fewness and their great numbers

celaleyn:42-42.t: ﴿إِذْ﴾ a badal (substitute) from يَوْمَ ﴿أَنْتُمْ﴾ were ﴿بِالْعُدْوَةِ الدُّنْيَا﴾ the nearer to Medina; it is with ḍamma and with kasra on the ʿayn: the side of the valley ﴿وَهُمْ بِالْعُدْوَةِ الْقُصْوَى﴾ the farther from it ﴿وَالرَّكْبُ﴾ the caravan, being in a place ﴿أَسْفَلَ مِنْكُمْ﴾ toward the sea ﴿وَلَوْ تَوَاعَدْتُمْ﴾ you and al-Nafīr, to fight ﴿لَاخْتَلَفْتُمْ فِي الْمِيعَادِ وَلَكِنْ﴾ He brought you together without appointment ﴿لِيَقْضِيَ اللَّهُ أَمْرًا كَانَ مَفْعُولًا﴾ in His knowledge, namely the victory of Islam and the obliteration of disbelief; He did that ﴿لِيَهْلِكَ﴾ disbelieve ﴿مَنْ هَلَكَ عَنْ بَيِّنَةٍ﴾ i.e. after a manifest proof established against him, namely the victory of the believers, despite their fewness, over the large army ﴿وَيَحْيَى﴾ believe ﴿مَنْ حَيَّ عَنْ بَيِّنَةٍ وَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لَسَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ﴾ Remember
